assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md documents 'Grouping strategy: **by-repository** — one Epic per repository.' and lists two Epics in the 'Epics to Create' table: 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. Tasks 1-2 are assigned to the backend Epic, Tasks 3-6 to the frontend Epic.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epics to Create table lists Epic summaries as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui', matching the prescribed format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: Each task file contains a '## Parent Epic' section. Tasks 1-2 (Repository: trustify-backend) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-backend'. Tasks 3-6 (Repository: trustify-ui) have 'Parent Epic: TC-9006: trustify-ui'. The impact-map.md Tasks tables confirm the same assignments.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md has an '### Incorporates Links' section: 'TC-9006 **incorporates** Epic "TC-9006: trustify-backend"' and 'TC-9006 **incorporates** Epic "TC-9006: trustify-ui"'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Incorporates links are set from the Feature to each Epic. Individual Tasks are children of their respective Epics, not directly linked to the Feature.'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md shows Tasks 1-2 under trustify-backend and Tasks 3-6 under trustify-ui. The Task Dependency Ordering section shows: Task 1 → Task 2 → Task 3 → Task 4 → Task 5 → Task 6, with the note 'Backend tasks (1-2) have lower numbers than dependent frontend tasks (3-6).' Individual task files confirm dependencies (e.g., Task 3 'Depends on: Task 2').

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Tasks 1-5 (non-documentation) each contain: Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create and/or Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections. Task 6 (documentation task, filename 'task-6-remediation-documentation.md') is exempt from Files to Modify/Create and Implementation Notes; it contains Repository (trustify-ui), Target Branch (main), Description, Acceptance Criteria (7 items), and Test Requirements (2 items).

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epics to Create table shows Issue Type 'Epic (level 1)' and Parent 'TC-9006' for both Epics. summary-comment.md Epics Created table confirms: 'Epic (level 1)' issue type and 'TC-9006' parent for both Epics.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All six task files contain a '## Repository' section with exactly one repository name: Tasks 1-2 have 'trustify-backend', Tasks 3-6 have 'trustify-ui'. No task contains multiple repository names.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All six task files contain: '## Target Branch' (all set to 'main'), '## Description' (substantive descriptions), '## Acceptance Criteria' (checkbox items), and '## Test Requirements' (checkbox items). Verified in task-1 through task-6 files.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: Six separate digest files exist, one per task: task-1-remediation-module-models-service-digest.md (sha256-md:800e5261b9938c7afe7a31c857a9c9377c0df4adcac6674273762b7c9dbc3cb2), task-2-remediation-rest-endpoints-digest.md (sha256-md:4befaa69686d5a20645fca3c49644bff8c0654ca3c6e3e3eef9df190131e1d42), task-3 (sha256-md:a21d4953c79d276de0fbcae3dfe0514e11385e0466beaa541814264d4fe4a949), task-4 (sha256-md:36a40be49caef6ead9f94f4a13474aecec10357cfc6abda154a5e7451ae0d86c), task-5 (sha256-md:739ba1d00886424772ccbc3646a80cf5f1f2ffa04411b7890e2003fb2e990021), task-6 (sha256-md:5f8b9cdc03c52dc995c36fa8f176f1f6171ca5b507fbca82c40be838157e1bd7). All use '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex>' format.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: Tasks 1-5 include convention rationale in the prescribed format. Examples: Task 1 has 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §Module Pattern: ... Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/mod.rs` matching the convention's Rust module scope.' and 'Per CONVENTIONS.md §Error Handling: ... Applies: task creates `modules/fundamental/src/remediation/service/remediation.rs` matching the convention's `.rs` scope.' Task 3 has 'Applies: task modifies `src/api/rest.ts` matching the convention's `.ts` scope.' No conventions are listed with 'Not applicable' annotations — only applicable conventions appear. Task 6 (documentation) has no conventions listed, correctly excluding inapplicable ones.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has Priority: Major. impact-map.md 'Inherited Field Values' section shows Priority: Major inherited by all Epics and Tasks. summary-comment.md confirms with a detailed table showing 'Inherited Priority: Major' for all six tasks and both Epics.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: Feature TC-9006 has Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (non-empty). CLAUDE.md has no '### Jira Field Defaults' section, so fixVersion scope defaults to 'both'. impact-map.md shows 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0' in the Inherited Field Values table. summary-comment.md confirms 'Inherited Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0' for all six tasks and both Epics.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in the outputs directory with title 'Inherited Field Propagation — TC-9006'. It contains a propagation table showing Priority (Major) and Fix Versions (RHTPA 1.5.0) propagated to 'All Epics and Tasks', plus detailed tables for Epics Created and Task Assignments showing inherited values per item. The impact-map.md also has an 'Inherited Field Values' section confirming the same.
